approaches.name: Multiply everything else for each position
approaches.intuition: For each position, multiply all the other elements. Division is avoided but every product is recomputed.

approaches.name: Prefix and suffix products
approaches.intuition: `answer[i] = (product before i) * (product after i)`. Two linear passes compute both without division.
steps: Left pass: store the running product before each index
Right pass: multiply the running product after each index
Apply the modulo at every multiplication
pitfalls: Zeros: this method needs no division, so they just work.
Negative numbers: reduce into `[0, 1000000006]` after every multiplication (in C++ and Java add the modulus when the remainder is negative).
Overflow: multiply in 64 bits before reducing.

talkTrackMd: Say why division fails (zeros and the modulus), then present prefix times suffix. Point out the O(1) extra space trick of reusing the output array for the left products.
